title.de: ERC 2025: Erweiterte lebensrettende Maßnahmen bei Erwachsenen

source.citation: Soar J, Böttiger BW, Carli P, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 Adult Advanced Life Support. Resuscitation 2025;215 Suppl 1:110769.
source.note: Read in full (2026-10-20) from a redistributed copy of the published PDF (certifico.com), through a fetch that quotes in pieces: near-verbatim, to be checked against the publisher's PDF when it can be opened. Compression rate and depth, 30:2 and the breath's duration are in the BLS chapter (Smyth et al., 110771), read the same way. The German texts are ours, in the GRC's terms where known; the GRC's own German text (Reanimation 2025 – Leitlinien kompakt) could be read only up to its BLS chapter.

pauseGap.means: A gap between compression onsets longer than this is a pause.
pauseGap.note: Studies of compression fraction count a pause from about 1.5–2 s without a compression; the guideline gives no definition. At 100/min compressions are 0.6 s apart.

pulseSystolic.means: An organised rhythm with a systolic pressure below this has no palpable pulse: CPR is needed (pulseless electrical activity).
pulseSystolic.note: A carotid pulse is felt from a systolic pressure of roughly 40–60 mmHg (bedside teaching, not well measured); the model's own step-3 placement put the pulse's end near 45.

title.en: Arrest team called at once, saying where

why.en: The defibrillator and the drugs come with the team. A call that does not say where sends them looking.
why.de: Defibrillator und Medikamente kommen mit dem Team. Ein Ruf ohne Ortsangabe schickt es auf die Suche.

rules.section: ALS: in-hospital cardiac arrest (call the resuscitation team; the team's response)
rules.note: The guideline asks for help to be called at once on recognising an arrest; 30 s from the collapse (time to check for breathing and say it) is ours. Saying where is scored because the scene delays a team that was not told (decision 8).

why.en: Compressions, the airway, the defibrillator and the drugs each need a pair of hands; a task nobody has been given is not done.
why.de: Kompressionen, Atemweg, Defibrillator und Medikamente brauchen je ein Paar Hände; eine Aufgabe, die niemand bekommen hat, wird nicht erledigt.

rules.section: Education: team competencies ("team leadership, task allocation, structured communication, and handovers")
rules.note: The guideline names task allocation as a team competency without a time; each task within 60 s of its becoming possible (compressions and airway from the collapse, defibrillator and drugs from their arrival) is ours.

title.de: Drückende Person etwa alle 2 Minuten gewechselt

why.en: Compressions get shallower within a couple of minutes, and the rescuer does not notice. Change at the rhythm check, so the change costs no extra pause.
why.de: Kompressionen werden innerhalb weniger Minuten flacher, ohne dass es der Helfer merkt. Beim Rhythmuscheck wechseln, dann kostet der Wechsel keine zusätzliche Pause.

rules.section: BLS: high quality chest compressions (change the person compressing about every 2 min)
rules.note: Every 2 min with 30 s tolerance, from when a second person could take over. The wording in the ERC 2025 BLS text is still to be checked; the model does not yet tire a compressor (its depth is not modelled).

why.en: Every second without compressions is a second without blood to the heart and brain. Recognising an arrest takes no more than 10 s.
why.de: Jede Sekunde ohne Kompressionen ist eine Sekunde ohne Blut für Herz und Gehirn. Das Erkennen eines Kreislaufstillstands dauert höchstens 10 s.

rules.section: BLS: recognition of cardiac arrest; high quality chest compressions
rules.note: The guideline says to start compressions as soon as the arrest is recognised and to take no more than 10 s to check breathing; 15 s from the collapse allows for the check and the first push. After seizure-like jerking at the onset, the clock starts when it stops ("Once the seizure stops, assess breathing", BLS).

why.en: Slower gives less flow; faster leaves too little time for the heart to fill.
why.de: Langsamer bringt weniger Fluss, schneller lässt dem Herzen zu wenig Zeit zum Füllen.

rules.section: BLS: high quality chest compressions ("Compress the chest at a rate of 100–120 min⁻¹ with as few interruptions as possible.")

title.en: Few interruptions: compressing at least 80 % of the time
title.de: Wenige Unterbrechungen: mindestens 80 % der Zeit Kompressionen

why.en: Coronary perfusion pressure builds over several compressions and is gone within seconds of stopping.
why.de: Der koronare Perfusionsdruck baut sich über mehrere Kompressionen auf und ist Sekunden nach dem Aufhören weg.

rules.section: BLS: high quality chest compressions ("with as few interruptions as possible")
rules.note: The guideline asks for as few interruptions as possible without giving a fraction; 80 % is the target used by resuscitation quality programmes (an assumption, to be sourced).

why.en: Every pause lets the pressure that fills the heart's own arteries fall within seconds. The guideline allows under 5 s for a shock and for intubation; two breaths take a few seconds more.
why.de: Jede Pause lässt den Druck, der die Herzkranzgefäße füllt, innerhalb von Sekunden fallen. Die Leitlinie erlaubt unter 5 s für einen Schock und für die Intubation; zwei Beatmungen brauchen ein paar Sekunden mehr.

rules.section: BLS: high quality chest compressions; ALS: defibrillation strategy, airway and ventilation
rules.note: Not in the ERC 2025 text read: it asks for as few interruptions as possible and sets under 5 s for defibrillation and for intubation, but no limit for the pause for two breaths. 10 s is the limit taught in earlier guidelines and courses (an assumption).

why.en: An arrest is recognised by unresponsiveness and absent or abnormal breathing: open the airway and look. Gasping is not breathing. A short burst of seizure-like jerking can be the first sign: once it stops, look at the breathing.
why.de: Ein Kreislaufstillstand wird an fehlender Reaktion und fehlender oder nicht normaler Atmung erkannt: Atemwege öffnen und hinsehen. Schnappatmung ist keine Atmung. Ein kurzer krampfanfallartiger Ausbruch kann das erste Zeichen sein: sobald er aufhört, die Atmung prüfen.

rules.section: ERC 2025 BLS: recognition of cardiac arrest
rules.note: The guideline's sequence: unresponsive, open the airway, look for normal breathing, then start compressions. Scored as a breathing check between the collapse and the first compression. A look while he is still jerking does not count (BLS: "Once the seizure stops, assess breathing").

why.en: If the chest does not rise with the breaths, look in the mouth and take out what blocks it; breaths that do not get in give no oxygen.
why.de: Hebt sich der Thorax bei der Beatmung nicht, in den Mund schauen und entfernen, was ihn verlegt; Beatmung, die nicht ankommt, bringt keinen Sauerstoff.

rules.section: ERC 2025 ALS: airway management during CPR
rules.note: Only in runs where the scenario puts a bolus in his pharynx (a teaching variant). The guideline asks for foreign material to be removed (suction, forceps under direct laryngoscopy) without giving a time; 60 s from the first breath that did not get in, or from the airway kit's arrival if that was later, is ours.

why.en: Before the airway is secured, compressions and breaths alternate 30:2.
why.de: Solange der Atemweg nicht gesichert ist, wechseln Kompressionen und Beatmungen im Verhältnis 30:2.

rules.section: BLS: rescue breaths ("alternate 30 chest compressions with 2 rescue breaths")
rules.note: Scored by the median count of the cycles ended by breaths, 27–33 (the tolerance is ours).

why.en: A quick squeeze gives less air and more of it into the stomach; a long one costs compression time.
why.de: Ein kurzer Druck bringt weniger Luft und mehr davon in den Magen; ein langer kostet Kompressionszeit.

rules.section: ALS: airway and ventilation ("Give each inspiratory breath over 1 s to achieve a visible chest movement.")
rules.note: The guideline: each breath over 1 s. Scored by the median of the learner's breaths, 0.6–1.5 s (the tolerance is ours).

why.en: The rhythm decides between a shock and more compressions; checking more often only costs compression time.
why.de: Der Rhythmus entscheidet zwischen Schock und weiteren Kompressionen; häufiger zu schauen kostet nur Kompressionszeit.

rules.section: ALS: defibrillation, energy levels and number of shocks ("Use single shocks followed by a 2-minute cycle of chest compressions.")
rules.note: The guideline's 2 min, with a tolerance of 20 s either way and the first check within 30 s of the pads going on (ours). A shock counts as a check.

title.en: Interruption for a shock under 5 s
title.de: Unterbrechung für den Schock unter 5 s

why.en: Charge while compressions go on; stop only to shock, then compress at once. The whole interruption, before and after the shock together, should be under 5 s.
why.de: Laden, während weiter komprimiert wird; nur für den Schock unterbrechen, dann sofort weiterdrücken. Die ganze Unterbrechung, vor und nach dem Schock zusammen, soll unter 5 s liegen.

rules.section: ALS: defibrillation strategy ("aiming for an interruption in chest compressions of less than 5 s"; continue compressions during charging; resume immediately after the shock)
rules.note: One limit for the whole interruption, not one before and one after.

title.en: No shock with hands on the patient, and none for a rhythm that is not shockable
title.de: Kein Schock mit Händen am Patienten und keiner bei nicht schockbarem Rhythmus

why.en: A shock through a rescuer injures them; a shock of asystole or a beating heart does nothing good.
why.de: Ein Schock durch einen Helfer verletzt ihn; ein Schock bei Asystolie oder schlagendem Herzen nützt nichts.

rules.section: ALS: defibrillation (safe delivery; shockable rhythms)

title.en: Adrenaline 1 mg after the third shock
title.de: Adrenalin 1 mg nach dem dritten Schock

why.en: In a shockable rhythm adrenaline comes after the third shock, not before: early shocks matter more.
why.de: Bei schockbarem Rhythmus kommt Adrenalin nach dem dritten Schock, nicht vorher: die frühen Schocks zählen mehr.

rules.section: ALS: medication and fluids, vasopressor drugs ("Give adrenaline 1 mg after the third shock for adult patients in cardiac arrest with a shockable rhythm.")
rules.note: Scored as given after the third shock and before the fourth; a dose given before the third shock in a shockable rhythm counts as early.

title.en: Adrenaline 1 mg as soon as possible in a non-shockable rhythm
title.de: Adrenalin 1 mg so früh wie möglich bei nicht schockbarem Rhythmus

why.en: Without a shockable rhythm there is nothing to shock: adrenaline is the one drug that can raise the pressure the compressions make, so it comes as soon as there is a line.
why.de: Ohne schockbaren Rhythmus gibt es nichts zu defibrillieren: Adrenalin ist das eine Medikament, das den Druck der Kompressionen erhöhen kann, also kommt es, sobald ein Zugang liegt.

rules.section: ALS: medication and fluids, vasopressor drugs ("Give adrenaline 1 mg as soon as possible for adult patients in cardiac arrest with a non-shockable rhythm.")
rules.note: Only in arrests whose rhythm was not shockable at the first look. The guideline says as soon as possible; 60 s from when it became possible (the rhythm seen, the drugs in the room, a cannula in) is ours: the time to draw up and give a prefilled syringe.

why.en: Its effect on the arterioles wears off within minutes (half-life about 2.6 min in arrest).
why.de: Die Wirkung auf die Arteriolen lässt innerhalb von Minuten nach (Halbwertszeit im Stillstand etwa 2,6 min).

rules.section: ALS: medication and fluids, vasopressor drugs ("Repeat adrenaline 1 mg every 3–5 min whilst ALS continues.")

title.en: Amiodarone 300 mg after the third shock
title.de: Amiodaron 300 mg nach dem dritten Schock

why.en: For VF that persists after three shocks.
why.de: Bei Kammerflimmern, das nach drei Schocks fortbesteht.

rules.section: ALS: antiarrhythmic drugs ("Give amiodarone 300 mg IV … who are in VF/pVT after three shocks have been administered.")
rules.note: Counted over all shocks for VF, whether the VF persisted or came back (the guideline: "irrespective of whether the shockable rhythms are sequential (refractory) or intermittent (recurrent)").

title.en: Amiodarone 150 mg after the fifth shock
title.de: Amiodaron 150 mg nach dem fünften Schock

why.en: A further dose for VF that persists after five shocks.
why.de: Eine weitere Dosis bei Kammerflimmern, das nach fünf Schocks fortbesteht.

rules.section: ALS: antiarrhythmic drugs ("Give a further dose of amiodarone 150 mg IV … after five shocks"; sequential or intermittent VF alike)

title.en: Thrombolysis when a pulmonary embolism is the suspected cause
title.de: Thrombolyse bei vermuteter Lungenembolie als Ursache

why.en: A clot in the lungs is a reversible cause, but only a lytic dissolves it, and slowly: give it early, then keep up CPR (the guideline says 60–90 min may be needed).
why.de: Ein Gerinnsel in der Lunge ist eine reversible Ursache, aber nur eine Lyse löst es auf, und zwar langsam: früh geben, dann die Reanimation fortführen (die Leitlinie nennt 60–90 min).

rules.section: ALS: medication and fluids, thrombolytic drugs ("Consider immediate thrombolytic drug therapy when pulmonary embolism is the suspected or confirmed cause of cardiac arrest." "In select patients with suspected pulmonary embolism, consider CPR for 60–90 min after administration of thrombolytic drugs.")
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is a pulmonary embolism. The guideline says immediate; 5 min from when it became possible (the collapse, the lytic in the room, a cannula in) is ours, to leave time to think of the cause.

why.en: Air trapped under pressure in the chest stops the blood returning to the heart: no compressions or drugs help until it is let out. A cannula through the chest wall on that side does it in seconds.
why.de: Unter Druck gefangene Luft im Thorax hält das Blut vom Herzen fern: Kompressionen und Medikamente helfen erst, wenn sie entweicht. Eine Kanüle durch die Thoraxwand auf dieser Seite schafft das in Sekunden.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.): "Always address hypoxia, hypovolaemia, electrolyte disorders, hypothermia, cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, thrombosis, and toxic agents"; in traumatic arrest, "Early and aggressive management of reversible causes (e.g. haemorrhage control, airway management, chest decompression) is essential for survival."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is a tension pneumothorax, and only the decompression of its side counts. The guideline gives no time; 2 min from when it became possible (the collapse, a cannula in the room) is ours. Read through a partial copy of the guideline: the chapter is to be read in full.

title.en: Fluids for an arrest from blood loss

why.en: A heart with nothing to pump cannot be compressed or drugged into an output: the volume lost has to go back in, fast, through a large line.
why.de: Ein Herz ohne Füllung kann weder durch Kompressionen noch durch Medikamente Auswurf erzeugen: das verlorene Volumen muss schnell über einen großen Zugang zurück.

rules.section: ALS: medication and fluids, fluids ("Give fluids during CPR only if cardiac arrest is caused by hypovolaemia." "Use either isotonic saline or balanced crystalloids for fluid infusion during CPR.")
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is hypovolaemia. The guideline gives no time; a bolus begun within 3 min of when it became possible (the collapse, the fluids in the room) is ours.

title.en: No fluid bolus unless the arrest is from blood loss
title.de: Kein Volumenbolus, wenn der Stillstand nicht durch Blutverlust kommt

why.en: In an arrest that is not from hypovolaemia, fluids do not help the heart and take hands and time from what does.
why.de: Bei einem Stillstand, der nicht durch Volumenmangel entsteht, helfen Infusionen dem Herzen nicht und nehmen Hände und Zeit für das, was hilft.

rules.section: ALS: medication and fluids, fluids ("Give fluids during CPR only if cardiac arrest is caused by hypovolaemia.")

why.en: Blood in the pericardium squeezes the heart until it cannot fill: compressions push on an empty heart. Draining even a little brings the filling back.
why.de: Blut im Perikard drückt das Herz zusammen, bis es sich nicht mehr füllen kann: Kompressionen drücken auf ein leeres Herz. Schon eine kleine Entlastung bringt die Füllung zurück.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.): "Always address hypoxia, hypovolaemia, electrolyte disorders, hypothermia, cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, thrombosis, and toxic agents"; in traumatic arrest, "patients with a cardiac tamponade need urgent thoracotomy"; ALS (Soar et al.): "POCUS may help identify treatable causes of cardiac arrest such as cardiac tamponade and tension pneumothorax."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is a tamponade. The guideline gives no time and, outside trauma, no procedure; a pericardiocentesis begun within 5 min of when it became possible (the collapse, the kit in the room) is ours.

why.en: Calcium does not lower the potassium, but within minutes it lets the heart's cells work again despite it: the bridge until the potassium falls.
why.de: Calcium senkt das Kalium nicht, aber es lässt die Herzzellen innerhalb von Minuten trotz des Kaliums wieder arbeiten: die Brücke, bis das Kalium fällt.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), hyperkalaemia: "Use IV 10 mL 10 % calcium chloride for patients with severe hyperkalaemia with ECG changes"; "the ERC continues to recommend the administration of IV calcium to patients with hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest in all settings"; "Give 10 units soluble insulin and 25 g glucose IV for treatment of moderate and severe hyperkalaemia."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is hyperkalaemia. The guideline gives no time; within 3 min of when it became possible (the collapse, the drugs in the room, a line in) is ours.

title.en: Insulin with glucose to lower the potassium
title.de: Insulin mit Glucose, um das Kalium zu senken

why.en: Insulin with glucose moves potassium into the cells: the most effective and reliable way to lower it quickly, though it takes tens of minutes.
why.de: Insulin mit Glucose verschiebt Kalium in die Zellen: der wirksamste und verlässlichste Weg, es rasch zu senken, auch wenn es Dutzende Minuten dauert.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), hyperkalaemia: "Use IV 10 mL 10 % calcium chloride for patients with severe hyperkalaemia with ECG changes"; "the ERC continues to recommend the administration of IV calcium to patients with hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest in all settings"; "Give 10 units soluble insulin and 25 g glucose IV for treatment of moderate and severe hyperkalaemia."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is hyperkalaemia. Within 5 min of when it became possible is ours.

why.en: With too little potassium, ventricular fibrillation keeps coming back after the shocks that end it. Potassium chloride, 20 mmol over 2–3 min and then 10 mmol, raises it while the algorithm goes on.
why.de: Bei zu wenig Kalium kehrt das Kammerflimmern nach den Schocks, die es beenden, immer wieder zurück. Kaliumchlorid, 20 mmol über 2–3 min und dann 10 mmol, hebt es an, während der Algorithmus weiterläuft.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), hypokalaemia: "Give 20 mmol potassium chloride IV/IO over 2-3 min, followed by 10 mmol over 2 min in hypokalaemic cardiac arrest"; "Where appropriate, replace potassium and correct magnesium deficit concurrently."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is hypokalaemia. Read through the Resuscitation Council UK text that cites the ERC. The guideline gives no time; the first 20 mmol run in within 5 min of when it became possible (the collapse, the drugs in the room, a line in) is ours: begun within 2–3 min. The follow-up 10 mmol is not scored.

title.en: Breaths with the bag for a patient who is not breathing
title.de: Beutelbeatmung beim Patienten, der nicht atmet

why.en: A heart starved of oxygen runs down into PEA and asystole; breaths bring oxygen back to it, and if they come before the arrest they may prevent it.
why.de: Ein Herz ohne Sauerstoff erlahmt bis zur PEA und Asystolie; Beatmung bringt ihm Sauerstoff zurück und kann, vor dem Stillstand, ihn verhindern.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.): "Always address hypoxia, hypovolaemia, electrolyte disorders, …"; asthma: "Treat life-threatening hypoxia with 100 % oxygen"; drowning: "Start with 5 ventilations using 100 % inspired oxygen when available".
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is hypoxia (a seizure, an opioid). Counted from the start of the scene, so breaths before the arrest count; within 60 s is ours.

why.en: Naloxone gives back the breathing the opioid took, but it takes minutes, and once the heart has stopped it does nothing for it: breaths first, naloxone alongside.
why.de: Naloxon gibt die Atmung zurück, die das Opioid genommen hat, aber es braucht Minuten, und wenn das Herz stillsteht, hilft es ihm nicht: zuerst beatmen, Naloxon daneben.

rules.section: ERC 2025 First aid (Djärv et al.): "ERC recommend that first aid providers administer naloxone to individuals with suspected opioid overdose"; "Naloxone is only effective for opioid overdoses and it can take several minutes to work"; "Naloxone is not effective once cardiac arrest has occurred." ERC 2025 Special circumstances: "Administer antidotes, where available, as soon as possible."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is an opioid. Counted from the start of the scene; within 3 min of when it became possible (the drugs in the room, a line in) is ours. In the scene a second responder can give it intranasally or IM; here IV.

title.en: Lipid emulsion for local anaesthetic toxicity

why.en: An antidote, given as soon as possible: lipid emulsion helps the heart to recover as the local anaesthetic leaves it. Recovery takes long: be ready to resuscitate for more than an hour, or to call for ECPR.
why.de: Ein Antidot, so früh wie möglich gegeben: Die Lipidemulsion hilft dem Herzen, sich zu erholen, während das Lokalanästhetikum es verlässt. Die Erholung dauert lange: auf über eine Stunde Reanimation oder eine ECPR eingestellt sein.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), toxic agents: "Administer antidotes, where available, as soon as possible"; local anaesthetic systemic toxicity: "Give an initial intravenous bolus of 1.5 mL kg-1 20% lipid emulsion followed by an infusion at 15 mL kg-1 h-1"; "Consider prolonged resuscitation (> 1 h) and ECPR."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is local anaesthetic toxicity. Read through the Resuscitation Council UK text that cites the ERC. The guideline says as soon as possible without a time; the bolus in within 3 min of when it became possible (the collapse, the drugs in the room, a line in) is ours. Repeat boluses, the doubled infusion and the call for ECPR are not scored.

title.en: No more than three shocks below 30 °C
title.de: Nicht mehr als drei Schocks unter 30 °C

why.en: A cold heart rarely responds to shocks; after three, the next one waits until he is warmer than 30 °C. Compressions go on.
why.de: Ein kaltes Herz spricht selten auf Schocks an; nach dreien wartet der nächste, bis er wärmer als 30 °C ist. Die Kompressionen gehen weiter.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), hypothermia: "Delay further defibrillation attempts if ventricular fibrillation (VF) persists after three shocks until core temperature is > 30 °C"; "Below 30 °C adrenaline will accumulate and may have more detrimental than beneficial effects"; "Rewarm hypothermic arrested patients with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO)."

why.en: Below 30 °C adrenaline is not cleared: it accumulates and may do more harm than good. It waits until he is warmer.
why.de: Unter 30 °C wird Adrenalin nicht abgebaut: es reichert sich an und schadet womöglich mehr, als es nützt. Es wartet, bis er wärmer ist.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), hypothermia: "Delay further defibrillation attempts if ventricular fibrillation (VF) persists after three shocks until core temperature is > 30 °C"; "Below 30 °C adrenaline will accumulate and may have more detrimental than beneficial effects"; "Rewarm hypothermic arrested patients with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO)."

why.en: A hypothermic heart is rewarmed back into a rhythm, not shocked into one: VA-ECMO rewarms him and carries the circulation meanwhile. Prolonged CPR is worth it, because the cold protects the brain.
why.de: Ein hypothermes Herz wird in einen Rhythmus zurückgewärmt, nicht geschockt: VA-ECMO wärmt ihn auf und übernimmt solange den Kreislauf. Lange Reanimation lohnt sich, weil die Kälte das Gehirn schützt.

rules.section: ERC 2025 Special circumstances (Lott et al.), hypothermia: "Delay further defibrillation attempts if ventricular fibrillation (VF) persists after three shocks until core temperature is > 30 °C"; "Below 30 °C adrenaline will accumulate and may have more detrimental than beneficial effects"; "Rewarm hypothermic arrested patients with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO)."
rules.note: Only in scenes whose cause is hypothermia. Within 5 min of the collapse is ours.
